days.summary: Today brings a redesigned Rokkan coach with team reviews, a reorganized notification bell, Career levels with cosmetics, new self-hosting controls, and broad speed-ups.

new.text: Turning matchmaking or a mode off now takes every lobby queued for it out of the queue. Ready checks already under way are left alone.

Rokkan reviews open in a full-width replay that starts paused on your first fix, with a menu to view the review as yourself, your team or a teammate. On wide screens the whole review fits one screen, with a list of every moment to jump between, and Space or K plays and pauses from anywhere on the page.

The match page shows a Rokkan Review band that moves through Queued, Reviewing and Ready, then previews the review's summary. The coach page lists each review as its match, marks unopened reviews as New with a filter for them, and the side menu counts your unopened reviews.

Teammates can see each other's Rokkan reviews from team matches on the team page's Coach tab and in a team view on the coach page. This view includes roster cards and team habits, with See All for the full list.
Administrators can open any team's or match's reviews in full. A team they opened but aren't on is marked with an Admin tag.
Every rated match now earns Career XP, and each level pays Stacks. Players unlock, buy or are granted cosmetics for their player card: banners, frames, nameplates and titles.

The cosmetics catalog has over 450 items, including an animated tier, and the Career Track now has rewards up to Level 1000. Administrators can grant items and Stacks to players, a team or a tournament's roster.
The bell is sorted into Needs you, Live now, New for you and Earlier. Alerts that resolve, such as a resumed map or a node back online, show their end state and move to Earlier.
A new "Clips of you" reel in the bell marks clips you haven't watched. Review notifications stack together, and content notices show a cover image.

On slim notification rows, clicking the dot marks the row read and double-clicking deletes it. The time turns into a menu that holds Delete. Administrators also get a gallery page with a sample of every notification type.

Panels installed with the 5Stack service get an update center where you choose Manual, Scheduled or When idle updates. Update Now runs a preflight check, shows live progress and pauses new matches until live ones finish.
Panels installed with the 5Stack service can also add game server nodes by code with an approval step. Settings gains Backup & Recovery, with nightly backups and Back Up Now, and a Diagnostics page.
Busy panels can run more than one replica of the API engine, placed on separate nodes where possible.

A checklist in the bell asks players to join the 5stack.gg Steam group and wear its clan tag in CS2, with a step-by-step guide in the FAQ. Once an imported match shows you wearing the tag, the card turns into a thank-you and stays that way.

improved.text: The Connect button on the Play schedule updates when a region switches to or from LAN.

An imported match's Steam message waits for its Rokkan review and is a single short line with the match link, without a large map preview. Rokkan review messages over Steam now go only to matches played outside 5Stack, and the duplicate in-app "Match Imported" notice is gone.

Disabled nodes that are online now get node file updates and Kubernetes maintenance changes, and show a dimmed amber dot while one is waiting. The "Node changes waiting" and "Kubernetes update available" alerts clear themselves once the work is done.
System Logs now includes the AI service that runs Rokkan, with its warnings and errors shown correctly.
Several pages are faster and lighter when many people view them at once.
Changes to other players' names, avatars and ranks now show up right away in lobbies, matches, invites and drafts. Your profile updates as soon as a gag or mute ends.

fixed.text: An administrator's coach inbox lists only their own reviews. The inbox no longer counts teammates' findings as yours.
Rokkan notices name maps the same way the site does.
Team cards show a space before "vs" in the Next and Last rows.
Invite notifications clear from the bell once the invite is accepted, declined or withdrawn.

Staff bells update live as role-wide alerts arrive, are dismissed or are deleted, and show only the alerts meant for them. Tournament registration invites now count toward the badge for a team's roster admins.
Steam messages that Steam delays or rate-limits are retried instead of lost, and are never sent twice.
Server owners can add themselves to a restricted server's player list.
A dedicated server keeps loading a plugin after its node auto-updates it.
Panels updated to the latest version finish starting up again.
After your role changes, the site picks up your new permissions right away without a reload.

days.summary: Today brings Rokkan, the AI coach, plus player and chat reports, team roster history, VAC Off matches and more control over what each game server node hosts.

new.text: Organizers can turn VAC off for a match from a new Server Launch card in Match Options. When the running server doesn't match the setting, the match page asks for a server reboot, and the VAC Off badge shows what the server is actually running.

Rokkan, 5Stack's AI coach, reviews your finished matches and scouts your next scrim or tournament opponent. A new Coach page lists your reviews, scouting and tendencies, each review moment opens the 2D replay at that round, and scheduled matches show a Rokkan briefing in their header.

Rokkan also reviews imported matches, and one verified player in a match unlocks reviews for every signed-in player in it. Reviews and scouting briefings also arrive as Steam messages for players who added a 5Stack bot as a friend.
Administrators can ask Rokkan to review any finished match from the match's actions menu.
Player profiles have a Teams tab showing the teams a player joined and left over time. Team pages show a roster history, and join and leave rows now appear in the team's activity feed.

Players can report someone they played with in the last 30 days from their profile or the scoreboard. Moderators handle each reported player as one case in a new Player Reports tab, and the reporter hears the outcome in the notification bell.

Players can report chat messages, and moderators handle them from a new moderation queue. Admins can set blocked words, which are masked in chat, and can turn on Rokkan chat moderation, which shows removed lines as "Message removed by Rokkan".

Each game server node can choose which match types it hosts and whether it takes practice servers, including nodes that host practice servers only. Highlight clips get their own GPU switch, separate from lineup renders.
Administrators can mark dedicated servers VAC Off. VAC-off matches only use on-demand servers or VAC-off dedicated servers, and other matches are never placed on VAC-off servers.

Nodes warn when they need a reboot to finish installing updates, including an NVIDIA driver that no longer matches the one loaded. Ubuntu nodes also warn when automatic security updates are off and show the command to turn them on.
The System Logs page shows how many times each service and pod has restarted. One click opens the run that crashed, with its exit reason, and you can download that run.
The header's update menu opens with a Needs attention list of node warnings, worst first. A node's inspector shows the fix for each warning, with a copy button for commands.
Self-hosted panels can opt in to deploying Rokkan, the AI service.
A changelog page at /changelog lists these daily summaries, with search and filters by kind and area across the whole history. It's linked from the user menu and the command menu.
The welcome page shows Scrim Finder, community servers, leagues and events as preview cards under Play and Compete. A new Run your own page shows what running your own 5Stack looks like.

improved.text: The practice server radar places markers with Valve's own map calibration. On Nuke, Train and Vertigo it switches to the lower-floor image while you stand on that floor.

Demo parsing records callouts for positions, kills and grenades. Round loadouts now show what players held when buy time ended, so late buyers no longer appear empty-handed, and a second flashbang is counted.
Radars are recalibrated for every map, and bomb-site markings follow each site's actual bounds.
Leaderboards filtered by source or role load much faster, and the player panel shows K/D and HS% ranks again.
Region pickers in match options, tournament stages, quick queue and practice only offer regions that can host that match type. A LAN match can't be saved when no LAN region hosts its type.
Pressing Update Now closes the update menu and starts the spinner straight away. A page refresh still shows the update running, so it isn't started twice.

Signed-in pages put much less load on the site. All your open tabs share one live connection, and the parts of every page that follow you, such as invites, lobby, teams, notifications and your matches, are fetched again only when they change.

The web app, API, demo parser, node connector, game streamer and browser extension move to the run-only 5Stack License. 5Stack stays free to self-host, and earlier versions keep their previous licenses.

fixed.text: A map being played no longer drops back to warmup when an older status arrives late. A map's result is no longer lost when the end of the map arrives out of order.
A live match's header no longer says "Auto Canceling" while a map is being played. During warmup and between maps it shows a deadline instead.

Matches on a dedicated server hosted on a 5Stack node no longer offer Reboot Server, and they show Offline rather than Booting when the server drops. The server picker now shows the server instead of a region.
When you link your match history, the newest match reliably gets its review, and older matches from the backlog are no longer reviewed.
Live streams of a series with workshop maps no longer stall on CS2's download prompt when the match moves to map 2 or 3.
Rendered highlight clips get their thumbnail again.
The node connector keeps running when a game server drops its connection, a demo can't be read or a network interface disappears.
Node warnings that aren't about the CPU are no longer labelled as CPU problems.
Update checks now include the AI service on installs that have it set up, so it stays up to date.
System Logs downloads of a pod with several containers, or of several pods, work again. A download whose log drops partway now fails instead of hanging.
The site stays up when an unexpected error happens, including when someone closes a log view or leaves partway through downloading an avatar, clip or image.
Chat rooms now share only the name, avatar and status that chat shows for each member.
The match page preview on the welcome page no longer captures the mouse wheel.

days.summary: Today brings AMD GPU support and Traefik routing for self-hosted panels, season ELO that includes tournament matches, demo uploads for every signed-in player, and speed-ups across the site.

new.text: The match scoreboard lists players by ADR in every view, rows glide to their new places when the order changes, and stat numbers roll like an odometer.

The event leaderboard has an ELO Gained tab that ranks players by how much the event's matches raised or lowered their rating. Voided matches don't count, and the tab follows the game mode the board is filtered to.
Who can upload demos is now a setting in demo settings, next to who can watch them. By default every signed-in player can upload a .dem file from their own profile.

The panel now routes traffic through Traefik, replacing the previous ingress controller, which is no longer maintained. Updating hands the web ports over automatically, installs behind a reverse proxy keep answering on 443 as before, and the ports guide has moved under the install guides.

AMD GPU nodes are supported for live streams, demo playback, highlights and utility lineups. Support is full on Strix Halo and experimental on other Radeon GPUs, with one GPU vendor per cluster. The setup script labels AMD nodes and asks whether to include integrated GPUs, and the GPU guides walk through it.
Plugins can ship Traefik routes alongside their existing install. On Traefik panels these routes are used, and a plugin's old routes are removed only once the new ones are working.

improved.text: Demo uploads are limited per player, and an upload you start can always be cancelled. Uploads from players who aren't administrators change only the uploader's own Premier rating and are processed after other imports.

Tournament matches now count toward the season they're played in, so a player's season ELO includes their events. Exclude Tournaments on the season leaderboard leaves out tournament results, and affected seasons are re-rated automatically a few minutes after updating.
A running Kubernetes update shows a progress bar, the version it is updating to and how many nodes are done. It can no longer be stopped part way, which would leave nodes on different versions.
Pressing Update Now in the header's update popover shows Updating and closes the popover, and the header icon spins until the services finish.
Adding a game server node now explains why it failed when the node's network setup is refused, and says when the cause is your network plan or billing.
The requirements guide now says the smallest recommended panel size of 4 cores and 8 GB handles up to 1,000 people online.
The notification bell, friends list, "my matches" banner, live match lists, tournaments and the rest of what every signed-in page shows now appear right away instead of after about a second.

Many parts of the site are faster, especially on busy panels: the notification bell, the friends list, the "my matches" banner, the nav's live match count, profile and team highlights, the matches list, the Play page's server list, practice sessions and tournament rosters.

fixed.text: If the demo upload setting holds an invalid value, uploads stay available to administrators, and their profile shows the upload option instead of hiding it from everyone.
The stream HUD shows each team's name on the side that team actually plays. The map-end banner and series score now go to the right team.

Live streams, demo playback and highlight clips on workshop maps no longer get stuck on CS2's workshop download prompt. The map now downloads before the game starts, and the startup steps show that download in the right order.
Rebuilding ratings no longer drops tied matches.
On Ubuntu 26.04 game nodes, ending a match or a dedicated server stops its CS2 server again.
Panels on Ubuntu 26.04 start correctly again, including the database and core services.
The Kubernetes update no longer counts offline nodes it will skip, and doesn't offer an update when only offline nodes are behind.
A GPU node's failed shader preparation stays marked as failed instead of disappearing a few seconds later.
The GPU node state shows the boot step's progress with a space before it, as in "Processing Vulkan shaders (1%)".

The guide for moving off the lowlatency kernel now removes the other lowlatency kernels first, so the node reboots into the generic kernel. It also warns about GPU nodes whose NVIDIA driver would be affected.
The notification bell, highlights and the "my matches" banner no longer keep showing outdated information when something changes while they are loading.
